questions.questionText: hour Additional Materials: Multiple Choice Answer Sheet Soft clean eraser Soft pencil (type B or HB is recommended) READ THESE INSTRUCTIONS FIRST Write in soft pencil. Do not use staples, paper clips, highlighters, glue or correction fluid. Write your name, Centre number and candidate number on the Answer Sheet in the spaces provided unless this has been done for you. There are thirty questions on this paper. Answer all questions. For each question there are four possible answers A, B, C and D. Choose the one you consider correct and record your choice in soft pencil on the separate Answer Sheet. Read the instructions on the Answer Sheet very carefully. Each correct answer will score one mark. A mark will not be deducted for a wrong answer. Any rough working should be done in this booklet.

The schedule shows the total utility derived by a consumer of a good X at different levels of consumption. quantity of X consumed 1 2 3 4 5 6 7 total utility (units) 30 50 65 75 80 83 84 The consumer obtains three units of utility from the last $ she spends on each good that she purchases. What is the maximum number of units of X that she will consume if the price of X is $5?

The line RS in the diagram shows the different combinations of goods X and Y that a consumer can afford with his present income. R N quantity of Y M S O quantity of X The consumer’s original equilibrium is at M. What could explain a change in his equilibrium position to N?

options.B: a decrease in the price of X and a bigger percentage increase in the price of Y
options.C: an increase in the price of X and an increase in his income
options.D: equal percentage increases in his income and in both prices

questions.questionText: A firm in a perfectly competitive industry employs two factors of production, X and Y. The table shows the factor price and the current marginal physical product of these two factors. factor X factor Y factor price $2.50 $6.00 marginal physical product 2 8 If the firm sells its product for $1 and aims to maximise profits, what should it do?

options.A: employ less of both X and Y
options.B: employ less of X and more of Y
options.C: employ more of both X and Y
options.D: employ more of X and less of Y

questions.questionText: In the diagram, the curve shows the various combinations of labour and capital that can be employed to produce a given level of output.

options.C: an increase in labour productivity
options.D: an increase in wage rates

questions.questionText: To increase its labour force from 100 to 101 workers, a firm has to increase the daily wage rate from $300 to $302. What is the marginal cost of labour per day?

The diagram shows a worker’s supply of labour curve. S wage rate per hour y W x z 0 10 20 30 40 hours per week The worker is required to work a minimum of 40 hours a week at the hourly wage, 0W. Which area measures the economic rent obtained by the worker?

options.A: x – y B x + y C y – x D y + z

questions.questionText: The diagram shows a firm’s short-run marginal cost curve. SRMC cost O Q output What explains why the curve is upward sloping at output levels above OQ?

options.C: rising fixed costs
options.D: the law of variable proportions

questions.questionText: The diagram shows a firm’s cost and revenue curves. MC $ AC O MR Q AR output What could explain why the firm produces output OQ?

options.A: It is operating in a contestable market.
options.B: It is operating in a perfectly competitive market.
options.C: It is seeking to maximise profits.
options.D: It is seeking to maximise sales revenue.

questions.questionText: A firm wishes to acquire some of the consumer surplus its customers currently enjoy. How might it achieve this?

options.C: by setting a price that maximises revenue
options.D: by taking advantage of economies of scale

questions.questionText: A perfectly competitive firm finds that at its current level of output, marginal revenue is $2.00 and marginal cost is $2.50. If the firm is a profit maximiser, what will happen to its price and output? price output

options.C: unchanged decreases
options.D: unchanged unchanged

questions.questionText: The diagram shows the outcome when a perfectly competitive market is taken over by a monopoly. $ X AC MR D O quantity What does area X represent?

options.C: the resulting deadweight loss
options.D: transfer earnings

questions.questionText: A tax is said to be regressive when

options.A: low income earners pay a higher proportion of their income in tax than high income earners.
options.B: marginal tax rates exceed average tax rates.
options.C: the cost of collecting the tax exceeds the revenue raised.
options.D: the marginal rate of tax is higher for high income earners than low income earners.

questions.questionText: Which is not a policy designed to correct market failure?

options.C: minimum wage policy
options.D: regulations to limit river pollution

questions.questionText: What is meant by ‘real wages’?

options.A: the marginal physical product of labour
options.C: the purchasing power of money wages
options.D: wages net of tax

questions.questionText: What is not a leakage from the circular flow of income?

options.C: undistributed profits
options.D: unemployment benefits

questions.questionText: According to Keynesian theory, when will an increase in the money supply leave the level of output unchanged?

options.A: when the liquidity trap is operative
options.B: when the money supply increase was not anticipated
options.C: when there is a floating exchange rate
options.D: when there is an immediate adjustment to expectations about future price levels

questions.questionText: According to monetarist theory, what will be the short-run and the long-run effect of an unexpected increase in the money supply on the real wage level? short-run long-run

options.C: unchanged increase
options.D: unchanged unchanged

questions.questionText: The diagram shows the relationship between consumption expenditure and income. C consumption O income Which statement is correct?

options.A: The average propensity to consume is constant.
options.B: The average propensity to consume is rising.
options.C: The marginal propensity to consume is equal to the average propensity to consume.
options.D: The marginal propensity to consume is less than the average propensity to consume.

questions.questionText: In a closed economy with no government the full employment level of income = $400 billion and the equilibrium level of income = $380 billion. If the deflationary gap is $4 billion, what is the marginal propensity to consume?
The diagram shows an aggregate demand curve. price level AD O national output What helps to explain why the curve is downward sloping?

options.A: When exports increase there will be an increase in national income.
options.B: When government expenditure increases there will be an increase in national output.
options.C: When investment increases there will be an increase in consumption.
options.D: When the price level increases there will be an increase in interest rates.

questions.questionText: An increase in the money supply leads to a fall in interest rates. What else will decrease as a result of these changes?

options.A: the desire to hold idle money balances
options.C: the price of government bonds
options.D: the velocity of circulation of money

questions.questionText: The diagram shows the market for loanable funds. D
Which feature of the Indian economy could explain why the purchasing power parity exchange rate of the Rupee is much higher than its market exchange rate?

options.A: high levels of duty on imported goods
options.C: the relatively low price of goods not traded internationally
options.D: the relatively low rate of inflation

questions.questionText: What is likely to be the effect of a fall in oil prices on the global economy?

options.A: a decrease in the rate of economic growth
options.C: a strengthening of cost-push inflation
options.D: a weakening of demand-pull inflation

questions.questionText: What is an unavoidable cost of long-run economic growth?

options.B: an increase in the working hours of the population
options.C: a sacrifice of potential present consumption
options.D: greater inequality in the distribution of income

questions.questionText: What could be expected to increase the pressure of demand-pull inflation in an open economy?

options.A: an appreciation of the foreign exchange rate
options.C: an increase in interest rates
options.D: the imposition of import controls

questions.questionText: When will taxes be most effective in dampening cyclical changes in national output?

options.A: when the tax yield is independent of national income
options.B: when the tax yield varies inversely with national income
options.C: when the tax yield varies less than proportionately with national income
options.D: when the tax yield varies more than proportionately with national income

questions.questionText: The government of a country decides to increase the proportion of its tax revenue it obtains from direct taxes and to reduce the proportion it obtains from indirect taxes. What is likely to be the impact on the distribution of income and on work incentives? distribution of work incentives income

options.C: more equal decrease
options.D: more equal increase
